title: personal-kpi-weekly-checkin-draft
body:
Week: 2026-02-22 -> 2026-02-28
Owner: Avery Chen (eng-serving-runtime) — personal OKR / weekly check-in (Wk9) — DRAFT

Context / high-level objective:
- Objective: Improve serving reliability and unit economics for the low-latency fleet so product teams can hit 99p latency SLOs with 15% lower per-token cost. This is my primary Q1/Q2 focus aligned with the Serving Runtime team OKRs.

Key Results (personal contributions I own / track):
1) Reduce 99p latency for 2 common prompt profiles (<=512 tokens) by 10% vs baseline (Jan 2026).
   - Baseline (Jan): 99p = 420ms (profile A), 99p = 610ms (profile B)
   - Current (end of week): profile A = 380ms (-9.5%), profile B = 560ms (-8.2%)
   - Notes: close to target on A, need another microkernel tweak + canary rollout for B.
2) Decrease per-token cost for low-latency pool by 12% via batching + prefix caching config changes on Dedicated shards I maintain.
   - Baseline cost: $0.012/token
   - Current estimate: $0.0108/token (~10% reduction) — still measuring at scale with synthetic workload.
3) Ship rollout plan + runbook for model fallback (hosted -> quantized variant) to keep availability during capacity events.
   - Draft runbook complete (internal doc). Canary policy PR opened.
   - Status: runbook = draft, PR = in_review (GH #198), need SRE review.

This week — progress summary:
- Performance: landed microkernel patch that improved profile A (bench results replicated on canary infra).
- Cost: adjusted batching window and enabled aggressive KV prefix caching on 2 Dedicated nodes; sim load shows ~10% cost drop but tail-latency needs more monitoring.
- Runbook/rollout: wrote initial runbook and templates for canary -> staged rollback; opened PR to add automatic metric gates.
- Collaboration: worked with Maya on telemetry dashboard (added latency breakdown by op type), synced with Jordan about autoscaler thresholds.

Open blockers / risks:
- Autoscaler interactions: current autoscaler policy sometimes scales up too late during bursty traffic; need a short-term tweak before full rollout. Blocker: need SRE approval for temporary policy change (blocked by on-call availability).
- Measurement noise: synthetic load differs from production distributions; need to run longer A/B to confirm cost improvements (cost measurement delayed by 2 weeks).
- PR review bandwidth: GH #198 needs at least one SRE + one infra-eng review to merge.

Next-week plan (concrete):
- Action 1: Schedule 1-hour SRE sync (Monday) to discuss temporary autoscaler policy; aim to get signoff or mitigation plan.
- Action 2: Run 48h production shadow experiment on 2 low-latency routes to validate per-token cost change and tail-latency (setup by Tuesday EOD).
- Action 3: Address feedback on GH #198 and incorporate metric gates; re-run unit tests and deploy to canary (by Thursday).
- Action 4: Draft customer-facing summary for product (one-pager) describing expected latency/cost SLO improvement and rollback plan (by Friday).

Personal development / non-KR goals:
- Mentorship: 2x 30-minute pairing sessions with junior eng (Siddharth) on perf debugging (completed).
- Writing: finalize a short technical note describing microkernel tradeoffs for our internal perf guild (drafted, needs editing).
- Health: protect one morning for focused deep work (blocked calendar on Tue/Thu).

Retrospective / notes to self:
- What went well: quick iteration on microkernel patch; better cross-team communication with Maya led to faster dashboard changes.
- What didn’t: underestimated time to get autoscaler temporary patch approved; next time start SRE engagement earlier.
- Experiment learnings: prefix caching gave bigger cost wins than expected but exposed tail-latency sensitivity; need to pair caching config with conservative latency gates.

TODOs (personal):
- [ ] Follow up on JIRA-RI-342 (autoscaler policy) — escalate if no response by Wed EOD.
- [ ] Push GH #198 after addressing test flakes.
- [ ] Create short demo video for product one-pager (5min).
- [ ] Add sample queries and prompt-length buckets to the telemetry dashboard (ask Maya for dashboard ownership change).

References / links:
- Perf dashboard: dashboard.redwood.internal/serving-runtime/latency-breakdown (ask Maya for view link)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/198
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ENG/Serving+Runtime+OKRs
- JIRA: JIRA-RI-342 (autoscaler policy)

Notes: This doc is a scratchpad. Will extract bullet items into the weekly standup update and move final runbook to Confluence once stable.

-- Avery
